# StegoRSA
## Description
A message has been encrypted using RSA. The public key is gone… but someone might have been careless with the private key. Can you recover it and decrypt the message?

Download the [flag](flag.enc) and [image](image.jpg).
## Hints
1. Metadata can tell you more than you expect.
2. Hex can be turned back into a key file.
## Solution
The file `image.jpg` is a photo of a key. Cute, but also a clue. Let’s run `exiftool` and see what we can see.

```console
% exiftool image.jpg
ExifTool Version Number         : 13.55
File Name                       : image.jpg
Directory                       : .
File Size                       : 21 kB
File Modification Date/Time     : 2026:06:08 22:22:12-04:00
File Access Date/Time           : 2026:06:09 20:40:37-04:00
File Inode Change Date/Time     : 2026:06:09 20:40:37-04:00
File Permissions                : -rw-r--r--
File Type                       : JPEG
File Type Extension             : jpg
MIME Type                       : image/jpeg
JFIF Version                    : 1.01
Resolution Unit                 : None
X Resolution                    : 1
Y Resolution                    : 1
Comment                         : 
Image Width                     : 512
Image Height                    : 512
Encoding Process                : Baseline DCT, Huffman coding
Bits Per Sample                 : 8
Color Components                : 3
Y Cb Cr Sub Sampling            : YCbCr4:2:0 (2 2)
Image Size                      : 512x512
Megapixels                      : 0.262
```

It looks like the `Comment` block is a bunch of hex data, specifically ASCII. Let’s convert it.

There it is. Decode `flag.enc`.

```console
% openssl pkeyutl -decrypt -in flag.enc -inkey <(exiftool -s3 -Comment image.jpg | xxd -r -p)
picoCTF{rs4_k3y_1n_1mg_51611ab8}
```

The flag is revealed: `picoCTF{rs4_k3y_1n_1mg_51611ab8}`
